title: Laplacian moments bounded by influence
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, let $f$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$ at every product outcome, and choose a coordinate $i$. For every real $p$ with $1\le p\le2$, the expectation of the $p$th absolute moment of the coordinate Laplacian is at most the influence of that coordinate: $\mathbb E_P|L_i f|^p\le I_i(f)$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to one
$f$ takes values in $\{-1,1\}$ at every outcome
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, a coordinate $i$, and $1\le p\le2$. Then $\mathbb E_P|L_if|^p\le I_i(f)$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $L_i h=h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h$; $I_i(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)^2$.
